introduction.text: Casino Nobile is a historic building within Villa Torlonia in Rome, notable for its neoclassical architecture, artistic collections, and its role as Mussolini's residence during the fascist era.

history.description: Restoration and enlargement of the Casino Nobile by Giuseppe Valadier, including stucco work and interior painting, carried out between 1802 and 1806.
Casino Nobile served as Mussolini's residence at Villa Torlonia, with added bunkers and modernizations, from 1925 to 1943.
Giovanni Raimondo Torlonia acquired the Vigna Colonna estate and commissioned restoration of its buildings.

design.description: Giuseppe Valadier designed the Casino Nobile's pronao, portico, loggia, and Ionic columns, creating a monumental entrance.
The fronton features a terracotta relief of Bacchus' triumph by Rinaldo Rinaldi.
The vestibule includes a coffered ceiling with gilded elements and putti, reflecting neoclassical style.

art.description: The Casino houses marble copies of the Amazone Mattei and a Fauno by Bartolomeo Cavaceppi.
Pietro Paoletti painted wall frescoes depicting mythological scenes such as Leda, Diana, and the Rape of Europa.
Giovan Battista Caretti contributed landscape paintings to the Casino's interior.
Francesco Podesti painted the Bacchus story frescoes in the Sala di Bacco.
Luigi Fioroni created Egyptian-inspired frescoes depicting Cleopatra and Marco Antonio.
